items.title: React 19 & Hooks Quick Reference
items.text: Concise reference covering useActionState, useOptimistic, Server Actions, useEffect pitfalls, and custom hooks.

cheatSheet.summary: React 19 revolutionizes full stack workflows by introducing first-class support for async Server Actions, automatic form handling with useActionState, and zero-lag optimistic UI updates.
keyTakeaways: Never call hooks inside conditionals, loops, or nested functions — keep them top-level.
useActionState replaces manual isSubmitting, error, and data state flags with native React form handling.
useOptimistic enables instant UI state feedback before the server round-trip completes.

items.title: Next.js App Router Architecture Guide
items.text: Best practices for route handlers, nested layouts, parallel routes, dynamic metadata, and SSR/SSG caching strategies.

cheatSheet.summary: Next.js App Router enforces server-first architecture. Pages and layouts execute on the Node.js server by default, drastically trimming client JavaScript bundle sizes.
cheatSheet.codeTitle: Next.js Route Handler with High-Performance Caching
keyTakeaways: Server Components cannot use browser hooks (useState, useEffect, onClick) — declare 'use client' at the file top when interactivity is required.
Utilize generateMetadata to inject dynamic page titles and OpenGraph tags for search engines.
Perform database queries directly inside Server Components to avoid redundant internal REST APIs.

items.title: RESTful API & Express.js Security Checklist
items.text: Hardening Node.js endpoints: CORS setup, rate limiting, JWT rotation, bcrypt password hashing, and input sanitization.

cheatSheet.summary: Production Node.js APIs must defend against automated bot scraping, denial of service (DoS), credential stuffing, and injection attacks.
keyTakeaways: Store JWT refresh tokens in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) theft.
Always hash user passwords using bcrypt (minimum 12 salt rounds) or Argon2.
Validate and sanitize every incoming payload using Joi or Zod schemas before running database logic.

items.title: JavaScript ES6+ Modern Syntaxes Cheat Sheet
items.text: Destructuring, spread/rest, Promises, async/await, Array methods (map, filter, reduce), and Event Loop mechanics.

cheatSheet.summary: ES6+ is the backbone of all modern frontend and backend frameworks. Mastering asynchronous pipelines and immutable transformations is essential for developer interviews.
cheatSheet.codeTitle: Modern ES6+ Syntax & Array Transformation Patterns
keyTakeaways: The JavaScript Event Loop gives higher priority to the Microtask queue (Promises) over the Macrotask queue (setTimeout).
A closure retains lexical scope access to outer variables even after the outer function has returned.
Use const by default and let only when reassigning; avoid legacy var.

items.title: Python for Data Science Quick Syntax Sheet
items.text: Pandas DataFrame indexing, NumPy array vectorization, Matplotlib plotting, and data cleaning routines.

cheatSheet.summary: Data Science workflows rely heavily on vectorized NumPy arrays and Pandas dataframes for fast in-memory tabular manipulation.
cheatSheet.code:
# Essential Data Science Routine
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Load & clean dataset
df = pd.read_csv("placement_records.csv")
df["salary"] = pd.to_numeric(df["salary"], errors="coerce")
df.dropna(subset=["salary"], inplace=True)

# Grouping & Aggregations
summary = df.groupby("domain").agg(
    avg_package=("salary", "mean"),
    total_placed=("id", "count")
).reset_index()

print(summary.sort_values(by="avg_package", ascending=False).head())
keyTakeaways: Never iterate over Pandas rows with iterrows(); vectorized NumPy operations run up to 100x faster.
Use df.loc[] for label-based indexing and df.iloc[] for zero-based integer positioning.
Impute missing values logically using .fillna() or interpolation instead of blindly dropping rows.

items.title: Prompt Engineering & LLM Interaction Guide
items.text: Zero-shot, few-shot, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), System Prompts, and output format structuring for GPT-4o & Claude 3.5.

cheatSheet.summary: Prompt Engineering transforms raw foundational models into deterministic, enterprise-grade AI applications by enforcing output schema and reasoning constraints.
cheatSheet.codeTitle: Structured JSON Prompt Template with Delimiters
cheatSheet.code:
### ROLE
You are a Principal Tech Interviewer at techcadd.

### TASK
Evaluate the candidate's answer for technical accuracy and clarity.

### CONSTRAINTS
Output strictly valid JSON matching this schema:
{
  "rating": number (1-10),
  "strengths": string[],
  "improvement_areas": string[],
  "ideal_answer_summary": string
}

### CANDIDATE ANSWER
"""[Insert Candidate Response Here]"""

### INSTRUCTION
Analyze step by step before emitting the final JSON object.
keyTakeaways: Use clear delimiter tags (e.g. ### or XML tags) to prevent prompt injection and separate context from instructions.
Providing 2-3 examples (Few-Shot Prompting) increases model adherence to complex output formats by over 40%.
Instructing models to 'think step by step' forces Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, drastically cutting math and logic errors.

items.title: RAG & Agentic AI Architecture Diagram
items.text: Vector embeddings, ChromaDB/Pinecone indexing, similarity search algorithms, LangChain agent loops, and CrewAI setups.

cheatSheet.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds LLMs in real-time, private documents without costly re-training, eliminating hallucinations.
cheatSheet.code:
# Minimal LangChain RAG Pipeline
from langchain_community.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings, ChatOpenAI
from langchain.chains import create_retrieval_chain
from langchain.chains.combine_documents import create_stuff_documents_chain

embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
vectorstore = Chroma.from_texts(
    ["techcadd provides comprehensive practical AI training in Lucknow."],
    embeddings
)
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 2})

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0)
# Documents retrieved -> injected into system prompt -> answered by LLM
keyTakeaways: Chunk size rule of thumb: 500-1000 tokens with a 10-15% overlap ensures semantic continuity across chunks.
Hybrid search combines BM25 keyword matching with dense vector cosine similarity for maximum retrieval precision.
Use cross-encoder rerankers (like Cohere Rerank) to score top 20 candidate chunks before feeding to the LLM.

items.title: SQL Queries & Database Modeling Guide
items.text: Window functions, complex CTEs, subqueries, indexing best practices, and Power BI relational schema modeling.

cheatSheet.summary: Advanced SQL forms the bedrock of data engineering and business intelligence. Window functions allow aggregated metrics across records without collapsing rows.
cheatSheet.codeTitle: SQL Common Table Expression (CTE) & Window Function
cheatSheet.code:
-- Top 3 Salaries per Department using CTE & Window Functions
WITH RankedStaff AS (
  SELECT 
    emp_id, 
    emp_name, 
    department, 
    salary,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank_in_dept
  FROM employees
)
SELECT department, emp_name, salary, rank_in_dept
FROM RankedStaff
WHERE rank_in_dept <= 3;
keyTakeaways: DENSE_RANK() does not skip rank numbers on ties (1, 2, 2, 3), whereas RANK() skips (1, 2, 2, 4).
CTEs (WITH clause) provide cleaner, more readable execution plans compared to deeply nested subqueries.
In data warehousing for Power BI or Tableau, organize dimensions around central fact tables (Star Schema) for fast analytical slicing.

items.title: Linux CLI for Ethical Hackers & Sysadmins
items.text: Bash scripting, file permissions (chmod, chown), network sockets (netstat, ss), SSH tunneling, and process monitoring.

cheatSheet.summary: Mastery of the Linux terminal is essential for cloud infrastructure engineering, penetration testing, server hardening, and automation.
cheatSheet.code:
# Network & Security Diagnostic Commands
ss -tulpn | grep LISTEN          # Check listening ports and PIDs
find / -perm -u=s -type f 2>/dev/null # Find SUID binaries for privilege checks
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa          # Restrict private key permissions
journalctl -u nginx -n 50 --no-pager # Inspect service logs

# Rapid subnet ping sweep
for ip in $(seq 1 254); do ping -c 1 192.168.1.$ip | grep "64 bytes" & done
keyTakeaways: File permissions: chmod 755 allows owner rwx and group/others rx. chmod 600 restricts access to owner read/write only.
Use kill -15 (SIGTERM) for graceful service shutdown; use kill -9 (SIGKILL) only when an unresponsive process must be stopped immediately.
Always monitor /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/secure for unauthorized SSH brute force access attempts.

items.title: OWASP Top 10 Web Vulnerability Matrix
items.text: Detecting and preventing SQL Injection, XSS, SSRF, Broken Access Control, and Insecure Deserialization.

cheatSheet.summary: The Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 lists the most critical web application security risks and remediation methods.
keyTakeaways: Broken Access Control is currently the #1 OWASP vulnerability — always verify user ownership on the server side.
Parameterized queries treat user input strictly as data parameters rather than executable SQL syntax.
Set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict flags on all authentication cookies to eliminate token theft via XSS.

items.title: Docker & Containerization Command Guide
items.text: Dockerfile directives, multi-stage builds, Docker Compose orchestration, volume mounts, and network bridges.

cheatSheet.summary: Docker standardizes application environments across development and production, packaging code, runtimes, system tools, and libraries into lightweight containers.
cheatSheet.code:
# Multi-Stage Production Dockerfile for Node.js
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=builder /app/package*.json ./
COPY --from=builder /app/.next ./.next
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
USER node
CMD ["npm", "start"]
keyTakeaways: Multi-stage builds eliminate heavy build tools and compilers from the final production image, slashing file sizes by up to 90%.
Never run production containers as root; specify an unprivileged user (e.g. USER node) in the Dockerfile.
Order Dockerfile commands with infrequently changing layers (package.json, npm install) first to maximize caching.

items.title: AWS Core Infrastructure & IAM Cheat Sheet
items.text: VPC subnets, Security Groups, IAM least-privilege roles, EC2 auto-scaling, and S3 lifecycle policies.

cheatSheet.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) powers modern enterprise cloud applications. Security, isolation, and cost optimization depend on proper IAM policy and VPC design.
cheatSheet.codeTitle: Least-Privilege IAM Policy for S3 Access
keyTakeaways: Enforce the Principle of Least Privilege: grant only the exact permissions needed; avoid 'Action': '*' in production.
Security Groups are stateful (inbound traffic automatically allows return outbound traffic); NACLs are stateless.
Keep databases and private backends inside Private Subnets, routing outbound traffic through a NAT Gateway in the Public Subnet.

items.title: AutoCAD 2D & 3D Command Shortcuts Matrix
items.text: 100+ keyboard shortcuts for drafting efficiency: layers, dimensions, isometric planes, blocks, and viewports.

cheatSheet.summary: AutoCAD remains the global industry standard for 2D technical drawings and engineering drafting. Shortcut keys are essential for drafting speed and precision.
cheatSheet.code:
=== Essential AutoCAD Speed Keys ===
L    -> Line            | PL   -> Polyline      | C   -> Circle
REC  -> Rectangle       | TR   -> Trim          | EX  -> Extend
O    -> Offset          | CO   -> Copy          | MI  -> Mirror
RO   -> Rotate          | F    -> Fillet        | CHA -> Chamfer
DLI  -> Dim Linear      | DAL  -> Dim Aligned   | LA  -> Layer Mgr
B    -> Create Block    | I    -> Insert Block  | F8  -> ORTHO Toggle
F3   -> OSNAP Toggle    | F10  -> Polar Snap    | F11 -> Object Track
keyTakeaways: Always assign entities to designated layers (WALLS, DOORS, DIMENSIONS, HATCH) with standard lineweights and colors.
Use Polylines (PL) for closed geometric contours so areas can be calculated and 3D extruded directly.
Keep Object Snap (F3) and Ortho (F8) enabled to guarantee accurate intersections without microscopic visual errors.

items.title: SolidWorks Parametric Modeling Checklist
items.text: Design intent rules, sketch constraint best practices, mate conditions in assemblies, and bill of materials (BOM) export.

cheatSheet.summary: Parametric 3D solid modeling captures design intent through geometric constraints, relationships, and parametric dimensions.
cheatSheet.code:
=== SolidWorks Engineering Checklist ===
1. Select optimal datum plane (Top/Front/Right) matching manufacturing orientation.
2. Anchor initial sketch directly to the Origin (0,0,0) for absolute reference.
3. Fully Define all sketches (Black lines only - never leave underdefined Blue lines).
4. Apply geometric constraints (Tangent, Concentric, Symmetric) before adding dimensions.
5. Create primary base solid feature first, followed by cuts, and apply fillets/chamfers last.
6. Fix only the ground component in assemblies; constrain other parts using Standard Mates.
7. Run Interference Detection before releasing 2D production drawings for fabrication.
keyTakeaways: Blue sketch lines represent under-defined geometry that will shift unpredictably when parent dimensions are modified.
Model symmetrical components using the Midplane extrude setting to maintain geometric symmetry for assembly mates.
Add cosmetic fillets and rounds at the bottom of the FeatureManager tree to prevent broken sketch reference errors.

items.title: Revit BIM Architecture Workflow Guide
items.text: Building Information Modeling levels, family creation, structural framing, wall schedules, and clash detection.

cheatSheet.summary: Building Information Modeling (BIM) in Revit creates parametric digital representations of physical buildings containing live material quantities, structural properties, and cost data.
cheatSheet.code:
=== Revit BIM Architectural Workflow ===
Phase 1: Configure Project Units (UN) -> Set True North and Project North.
Phase 2: Establish Building Levels in Elevation View (Foundation, GF, FF, Roof).
Phase 3: Set Structural Grid Lines (GR) for column and beam structural centers.
Phase 4: Draw Exterior Compound Walls with authentic material strata (Brick, Cavity, Insulation, Plaster).
Phase 5: Insert hosted Door & Window families (automatically cuts wall openings).
Phase 6: Create Floor Slabs with boundary profiles locked to structural wall cores.
Phase 7: Generate automated Material Takeoff Schedules & Bill of Quantities (BOQ).
keyTakeaways: Revit building elements are intelligent objects: modifying a door width in a 2D floor plan updates 3D elevations and schedules automatically.
Set up Worksets and a Central Model when multiple project architects and MEP consultants work on the same model file.
Run automated Interference Checks between Architectural, Structural, and MEP models to resolve service clashes before construction starts.

items.title: 3ds Max & V-Ray Photorealistic Rendering Guide
items.text: Polygonal modeling, PBR material creation, daylight lighting systems, camera composition, and V-Ray frame buffer settings.

cheatSheet.summary: Architectural visualization relies on physically based rendering (PBR) to simulate natural daylight, artificial interior illumination, and accurate material reflection.
cheatSheet.code:
=== V-Ray Photorealistic Rendering Pipeline ===
1. Set System Unit Scale to Millimeters (mandatory for optical light inverse-square falloff).
2. Configure V-Ray Physical Camera (Focal Length: 35-50mm, f-number: 8.0, Shutter: 1/125s).
3. Setup V-Ray Sun & Sky with authentic atmospheric turbidity and realistic intensity (0.05-0.10).
4. Assign PBR materials using Diffuse, Roughness, Normal, and IOR Refraction maps.
5. Set Global Illumination (GI) to Brute Force (Primary) and Light Cache (Secondary).
6. Enable V-Ray Denoiser in Render Elements to cut render calculation times by over 50%.
keyTakeaways: Accurate lighting depends on true scale: if a room is modeled off-scale, light decay and optical exposure will look artificial.
Control image brightness using the camera's physical exposure settings rather than unnaturally boosting light source multipliers.
Render passes in 16-bit or 32-bit EXR format to allow non-destructive post-production adjustments in Photoshop.
